column1: # CDIF CoreDiscovery to DCAT-AP 3 and GeoDCAT-AP 3. One row per top-level CDIF property.
# `how` names the function in app/dcat.py that writes the property; `lost` means DCAT-AP has no
# place for it and it is left out. A test fails if the profile schema gains a property not listed.
# profile: `all` for both outputs, `geodcat_ap` for GeoDCAT-AP only.

column5: DCAT-AP requires one. When the record has none, it is the title followed by "description missing".
The scheme (propertyID) is not carried; the value or its address is.
A vocabulary term is written as its label. Its vocabulary address is lost: dcat:theme accepts only terms of a registered theme scheme.
Author order is lost: RDF properties are unordered.
Any agent given only as an address, with no name anywhere in the record, is lost: DCAT-AP requires a name.
Written on each distribution, where DCAT-AP expects it, or on the dataset when there is no distribution.
Several conditions become labels of one rights statement.
Checksum, per-distribution provider and web service actions are lost.
A bounding box or point is carried; other geometry and place types are lost.
Only intervals written as start/end dates are carried; numeric time positions are lost.
Maintainer and source catalog are lost.
DCAT-AP needs a language address from the EU vocabulary; CDIF holds a code.
